title: Dry meat with paper towels before searing
content: Surface moisture creates steam which prevents a proper brown crust from forming. Patting meat completely dry helps it sear quickly and crisp evenly.
question: Why should you dry meat before searing it?
correct_answer: Moisture creates steam and prevents browning
wrong_1: It removes excess salt from the surface
wrong_2: It tenderizes the tough outer muscle fibers

title: Avoid crowding the pan when cooking
content: Adding too much food at once traps steam and lowers the pan temperature. Leave space between items so they brown instead of boiling in their own liquids.
question: What happens when you overcrowd a pan?
correct_answer: Food steams instead of browning
wrong_1: Food cooks twice as fast
wrong_2: The pan absorbs all the oil

title: Heat the pan before adding oil
content: Adding oil to a hot pan creates a smooth nonstick barrier and prevents food from sticking. Cold oil in a cold pan often absorbs into food instead of searing it.
question: Why heat the pan before adding oil?
correct_answer: It prevents food from sticking and absorbing excess oil
wrong_1: It changes the chemical taste of the cooking oil
wrong_2: It ensures the pan heats evenly on all sides

title: Do not rinse raw chicken before cooking
content: Rinsing raw poultry splashes bacteria across your sink countertops and nearby utensils. High cooking temperatures will kill any bacteria safely.
question: Why should you avoid washing raw chicken?
correct_answer: It splashes bacteria around your kitchen
wrong_1: It removes natural flavors from the meat
wrong_2: It causes the meat to become tough and dry

title: Salt pasta water generously before boiling
content: Adding enough salt to boiling water seasons pasta from the inside out as it absorbs liquid. Seasoning after cooking only coats the outside surface.
question: When is the best time to salt pasta?
correct_answer: In the boiling water before adding pasta
wrong_1: Only after draining the cooked pasta
wrong_2: When the pasta is cooling down

title: Save a cup of starchy pasta water
content: Starchy cooking water helps bind sauce to pasta and creates a smooth texture. Mix a few spoons into your sauce before combining it with the pasta.
question: How does leftover pasta water help a sauce?
correct_answer: It helps the sauce bind and emulsify smoothly
wrong_1: It acts as a preservative to keep sauce fresh
wrong_2: It lowers the overall calories of the dish

title: Preheat your oven fully before baking
content: Putting food in an unheated oven leads to uneven cooking and ruined textures. Wait for the oven to reach the target temperature before sliding food inside.
question: Why wait for the oven to preheat completely?
correct_answer: It ensures food cooks evenly at the right rate
wrong_1: It prevents food from catching on fire
wrong_2: It sterilizes the baking pans before use

title: Measure flour by spooning it into cups
content: Scooping flour directly with a measuring cup packs it down adding up to 25 percent extra flour. Fluff it spoon it in and sweep the top level.
question: What is the best way to measure flour by cup?
correct_answer: Spoon it into the cup and sweep the top flat
wrong_1: Scoop firmly from the bag and press it down
wrong_2: Sift it directly into a wet measuring liquid cup

title: Keep acidic ingredients away from raw garlic
content: Acid like lemon juice or vinegar stops raw garlic from mellowing out during cooking. Add acids near the end of cooking so garlic softens properly.
question: Why delay adding acid when cooking garlic?
correct_answer: Acid stops garlic from softening and mellowing
wrong_1: Acid turns garlic extremely bitter immediately
wrong_2: Acid prevents garlic from releasing its oil

title: Do not cook acid in unseasoned cast iron
content: Highly acidic foods like tomatoes or wine can strip the protective seasoning layer on cast iron pans. Use stainless steel or enamel for acidic dishes.
question: Why avoid cooking tomatoes in basic cast iron?
correct_answer: Acid can strip the pan's protective seasoning
wrong_1: Acid causes the pan to warp permanently
wrong_2: Acid makes the iron melt into the sauce

title: Dull knives are more dangerous than sharp ones
content: A dull blade easily slips off smooth vegetable skins and requires more force to cut. Sharp knives slice cleanly with minimal pressure and far less slipping.
question: Why is a dull knife considered unsafe?
correct_answer: It slips easily and requires more force
wrong_1: It dulls the cutting board permanently
wrong_2: It creates tiny metal shavings in food

title: Thaw frozen meat in the refrigerator
content: Leaving raw meat on the counter allows harmful bacteria to multiply on the warm outer layers while the core stays frozen. Always thaw in the fridge.
question: Where is the safest place to thaw frozen meat?
correct_answer: In the refrigerator overnight
wrong_1: On the kitchen counter at room temp
wrong_2: In a bowl of warm standing water

title: Store tomatoes at room temperature
content: Refrigerating whole fresh tomatoes damages their cellular structure making the flesh mealy and dulling natural flavors. Keep them stem-side down on the counter.
question: Why avoid putting whole fresh tomatoes in the fridge?
correct_answer: Cold temperature makes them mealy and dulls flavor
wrong_1: Cold temperature makes them ripen too fast
wrong_2: Cold temperature turns the flesh extremely bitter

title: Do not rinse cooked pasta with cold water
content: Rinsing pasta washes away surface starches that help sauces stick to the noodles. Only rinse pasta if you are making a cold pasta salad.
question: Why should you skip rinsing cooked pasta?
correct_answer: It removes starches that help sauce stick
wrong_1: It causes the pasta to break into pieces
wrong_2: It doubles the sodium content instantly

title: Taste your food while you cook
content: Waiting until serving to taste food makes it hard to correct seasoning or acidity. Taste regularly as you cook and adjust salt and spices in small steps.
question: Why taste food throughout the cooking process?
correct_answer: It allows you to adjust seasoning gradually
wrong_1: It speeds up the overall cooking time
wrong_2: It prevents ingredients from burning

title: Cut meat across the grain for tenderness
content: Slicing perpendicular to the direction of muscle fibers shortens the tough strands. This makes even cheaper cuts of meat much easier to chew.
question: How does slicing across the grain affect meat?
correct_answer: It shortens muscle fibers for a tender bite
wrong_1: It keeps the meat hot for a longer time
wrong_2: It seals the juices inside the steak

title: Soak cut potatoes before frying or roasting
content: Rinsing or soaking raw potato pieces removes excess surface starch. This prevents them from sticking together and helps them get extra crispy when cooked.
question: Why soak raw cut potatoes in cold water?
correct_answer: To remove surface starch for crispier results
wrong_1: To cook them halfway before heating
wrong_2: To absorb extra moisture into the core

title: Add delicate fresh herbs at the very end
content: Soft herbs like basil parsley and cilantro lose their vibrant flavor and color under heat. Stir them in just before serving for maximum freshness.
question: When should soft herbs like basil be added?
correct_answer: Right before serving the dish
wrong_1: At the beginning with the onions
wrong_2: Halfway through a long simmer

title: Never pour water on a grease fire
content: Water instantly vaporizes in hot oil throwing burning fat everywhere and expanding the flames. Cover the pan with a metal lid or use baking soda.
question: What should you do if a pan of oil catches fire?
correct_answer: Smother it with a metal lid or baking soda
wrong_1: Pour cold water directly into the pan
wrong_2: Blow hard on the flames until extinguished

title: Do not overmix pancake and muffin batter
content: Stirring batter too much develops gluten strands making baked goods tough and rubbery. Mix just until dry ingredients are moistened leaving small lumps.
question: What happens when pancake batter is overmixed?
correct_answer: The pancakes become tough and rubbery
wrong_1: The batter turns too thin to cook properly
wrong_2: The pancakes cook into flat crispy chips

title: Use a liquid measuring cup for wet ingredients
content: Dry measuring cups require filling to the rim which leads to spills when measuring liquids. Clear liquid cups let you read volume at eye level easily.
question: Why use clear spout cups for liquids?
correct_answer: They allow accurate level reading without spilling
wrong_1: They hold more weight than plastic dry cups
wrong_2: They keep liquids at room temperature longer

title: Bring eggs to room temperature before baking
content: Cold eggs straight from the fridge can curdle warm butter mixtures and cause uneven rising. Place eggs in warm water for 5 minutes before using.
question: Why use room temperature eggs in baking?
correct_answer: They mix smoothly without curdling butter
wrong_1: They double the total protein in recipes
wrong_2: They prevent sugar from dissolving too fast

title: Add garlic after onions have softened
content: Garlic burns easily because of its high sugar content and small size. Cook onions first then add garlic for the last minute to avoid a burnt taste.
question: Why add garlic after onions are already softened?
correct_answer: Garlic burns much faster than onions
wrong_1: Garlic needs onions to activate its flavor
wrong_2: Garlic absorbs all the oil instantly

title: Balance overly salty dishes with acid or sweet
content: If a dish gets too salty adding a splash of vinegar lemon juice or a pinch of sugar balances the taste perception without diluting the entire pot.
question: How can you fix a dish that tastes slightly too salty?
correct_answer: Add a splash of lemon juice or sugar
wrong_1: Add a spoonful of baking powder
wrong_2: Double the amount of oil in the pan

title: Let cooked vegetables drain before stir-frying
content: Wet vegetables drop the skillet temperature and steam instead of searing. Drain and dry boiled or washed veggies before throwing them in a hot wok.
question: Why dry vegetables before adding to a high-heat wok?
correct_answer: To prevent them from steaming instead of searing
wrong_1: To keep them from absorbing vegetable oil
wrong_2: To preserve their natural salt content
